weakness.title: Insufficient Resistance of Openings to Forced Entry
weakness.description: An opening in the boundary of a protected area offers less resistance to forced entry than the sensitivity of the area requires.

extended_description.applicability: Doors, windows, hatches, shutters, skylights, vents, service openings and any other opening through which a person could pass or reach into a protected area, including their frames, hinges, glazing, panels and surrounding structure. The resistance required depends on the sensitivity of the area and on the time an attacker can be expected to need before being detected or stopped.
extended_description.exploitation: An unauthorized person passes through an opening by breaking, removing or otherwise overcoming it with physical means, because its construction offers little resistance or because a weak point in the frame, the glazing, the hinges or the surrounding structure can be attacked instead.

row.details: Entry control is bypassed without a valid credential.
Unauthorized persons reach information, media and equipment inside the area.
Equipment can be altered by persons who gained entry by force.

row.description: Choose doors, windows, frames and glazing with a rated resistance suited to the sensitivity of the area.
Treat the leaf, frame, hinges, glazing and surrounding wall as one assembly, and strengthen its weakest part.
Give windows, hatches, vents and service openings a resistance equivalent to that of the main entrance, and fit bars or grilles to those that are not meant for passage.
Add detection and response, because no barrier resists indefinitely.
Check construction regularly, and replace worn or damaged parts.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-3 Physical Access Control
ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A: 7.1 Physical security perimeters, 7.3 Securing offices, rooms and facilities
